explanations.explanation: True, friend. The expert in the law, a man who knows God's Law, asks his big question. Jesus hands one right back: “What is written in the Law?” (Luke 10:26). I think the man came to do the quizzing and suddenly he's the one with the pop quiz.

Jesus doesn't answer straight out. He replies, “What is written in the Law?” and then asks, “How do you read it?” (Luke 10:26). So the expert gets a question back instead of an answer. That makes True the right pick here.

explanations.answer: Loving God and loving your neighbor
explanations.explanation: That's the pair. The expert says to love the Lord your God with everything you've got, and to “Love your neighbor as yourself.” Two commands, one about God and one about the person next to you. Hang onto that second one, because the whole story is about to lean on it.

explanations.answer: Keeping the Sabbath and giving offerings
explanations.explanation: The Sabbath and offerings are part of the Law (Exodus 20:8; Leviticus 1:2), but they aren't what the expert says here. He answers with loving the Lord your God with heart, soul, strength and mind. Then he adds loving your neighbor as yourself. Neither the Sabbath nor offerings came out of his mouth.

explanations.answer: Honoring parents and telling the truth
explanations.explanation: Those are good commands, friend, and they're in the Law too (Exodus 20:12, 16). But the expert doesn't quote them here. He quotes loving the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, strength and mind, and loving your neighbor as yourself. Both of his commands are about love.
Jesus doesn't point out anything missing. He says, “You have answered correctly…” (Luke 10:28). So the expert's answer stands just as he gave it. That makes this one False.

False is right. Jesus tells the expert, “You have answered correctly…” (Luke 10:28). He doesn't add anything or take anything away. The expert had the answer, and now the question is what he'll do with it.
Do. Jesus says, “Do this and you will live.” (Luke 10:28). Not just know it, not just say it, do it. I've memorized plenty of recipes in my day, and not one of them ever baked itself.
Memorizing isn't the word Jesus uses. He says, “Do this and you will live.” (Luke 10:28). The word is do. Saying the commands is one thing, and doing them is what Jesus asks.

Teaching is a fine thing, friend, but it isn't the word Jesus uses. He tells the expert, “Do this and you will live.” (Luke 10:28). The answer is do. The expert is a man who studies the Law, so this one lands right on him.
Yes, he asks, “And who is my neighbor?” The text says he wanted to justify himself (Luke 10:29). So the man who gave the right answer asks one more question. I think a lot of us know that feeling.

explanations.answer: And how often should I pray
explanations.explanation: Prayer is a good question, but it isn't the one he asks. After Jesus says he answered correctly, the expert asks, “And who is my neighbor?” (Luke 10:29). That question is about the second command he quoted. It's the one that gets a story.
He doesn't ask that, friend. What he asks is, “And who is my neighbor?” (Luke 10:29). The text says he wanted to justify himself. Nothing in his question is about ranking laws.

explanations.answer: He passes by on the other side
explanations.explanation: That's what Jesus says. The priest, a man who served in God's house, saw the man and “…passed by on the other side.” (Luke 10:31). Jesus doesn't tell us why. He just tells us what the priest did, and I think that picture is enough.

explanations.answer: He runs to the next town for help
explanations.explanation: No running here, friend. Jesus says the priest saw the man and “…passed by on the other side.” (Luke 10:31). Nobody goes for help in this part of the story. The man is still lying there when the priest is gone.

explanations.answer: He stops and prays over the man
explanations.explanation: No stopping to pray in this story. Jesus says that when the priest saw the man, “…he passed by on the other side.” (Luke 10:31). Prayer isn't mentioned. Passing by is what Jesus says he did.
The Levite passes by. Jesus says that when he came to that spot and saw the man, “…he passed by on the other side.” (Luke 10:32). That's what the priest did too (Luke 10:31). So the answer is False.

False is right, baker. Jesus says a Levite, a man from the tribe of Levi, came to that spot and saw the man, and “…he passed by on the other side.” (Luke 10:32). He keeps on walking, just like the priest before him (Luke 10:31). Two men came by, and neither one stopped.

explanations.answer: He goes to him and bandages his wounds
explanations.explanation: He goes right to him. The Samaritan, a man from Samaria, has compassion, then “…went to him and bandaged his wounds…” (Luke 10:34). The compassion comes first, and then he goes to the man.

explanations.answer: He calls out for anyone nearby to help
explanations.explanation: Calling out for help isn't what Jesus says. The Samaritan, a man from Samaria, “…went to him and bandaged his wounds…” (Luke 10:34). Jesus doesn't mention him calling for anyone. He goes to the man and bandages him.

explanations.answer: He gives him his cloak and keeps going
explanations.explanation: He doesn't keep going, friend. The Samaritan, a man from Samaria, has compassion, then “…went to him and bandaged his wounds…” (Luke 10:34). He stays, and the story shows him doing a lot more than that. A cloak never comes up.

explanations.answer: He puts him on his own animal
explanations.explanation: That's it. The Samaritan “…put him on his own animal…” (Luke 10:34). It's his own animal, not somebody else's. I think that's a generous thing to share.

explanations.answer: He carries him on his back
explanations.explanation: No carrying on his back here. Jesus says the Samaritan “…put him on his own animal…” (Luke 10:34). Carrying the man on his back isn't mentioned. The animal is how the man gets to the inn.

explanations.answer: He waves down a passing cart
explanations.explanation: No cart shows up in this story, friend. The Samaritan “…put him on his own animal…” (Luke 10:34). He uses what he has with him. It's his animal, and it's the hurt man's ride now.

An inn is right. The Samaritan puts the man on his animal and “…brought him to an inn…” (Luke 10:34). An inn is a place for travelers to stay. The road was no place to leave a man half dead, and the Samaritan didn't.
The temple never comes up in this story, friend. Jesus says the Samaritan “…brought him to an inn…” (Luke 10:34). An inn is a place where travelers stay. That's where the hurt man ends up.
A synagogue isn't in this story. Jesus says the Samaritan “…brought him to an inn…” (Luke 10:34). An inn is a place where travelers stay. That's where the care continues.
True. Jesus says the Samaritan “…took care of him.” (Luke 10:34). He didn't just drop the man off at the door. He stayed and looked after him, and the next day we see him paying the innkeeper.

The text says otherwise, friend. At the inn the Samaritan “…took care of him.” (Luke 10:34). He doesn't just hand the man over and walk out. He stays with him and looks after him, so True is the answer.

explanations.answer: Take care of him and I will repay you
explanations.explanation: That's his promise. He tells the innkeeper, “Take care of him…” and “…on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.” (Luke 10:35). He pays two denarii up front and says he'll cover whatever else comes up. I think that innkeeper got a pretty easy customer.

explanations.answer: Send him home when he can walk
explanations.explanation: He says nothing about sending the man anywhere. He tells the innkeeper, “Take care of him…” and promises, “…on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.” (Luke 10:35). The Samaritan's concern is the man's care. He's paying for it too.

explanations.answer: Find out who did this to him
explanations.explanation: Finding out who did it isn't what he says, friend. The Samaritan tells the innkeeper, “Take care of him…” and says he'll repay any additional expense when he returns (Luke 10:35). Jesus doesn't mention the robbers in what he says. Everything he says to the innkeeper is about the man's care.

explanations.answer: The one who showed him mercy
explanations.explanation: That's what the expert says: “The one who showed him mercy…” (Luke 10:37). He never says the word Samaritan, but he points straight at the man who stopped. Remember, he started out asking who his neighbor is. Now he's answering who acted like one.

The priest isn't who the expert picks. Jesus says the priest “…passed by on the other side.” (Luke 10:31). The expert answers, “The one who showed him mercy…” (Luke 10:37). That's the man who stopped and helped.
The Levite isn't his answer either, friend. He “…passed by on the other side.” (Luke 10:32). The expert says, “The one who showed him mercy…” (Luke 10:37). That's the one who actually helped the man.
Yes. Jesus tells him, “Go and do likewise.” (Luke 10:37). Go back to what Jesus said earlier: “Do this and you will live.” (Luke 10:28). The story ends with a job, not a test score.
Jesus doesn't send him off to teach. He says, “Go and do likewise.” (Luke 10:37). Do what the one who showed mercy did. The expert knows the Law well, but this time Jesus points him toward acting.
No sacrifice is mentioned, friend. Jesus says, “Go and do likewise.” (Luke 10:37). He means do what the one who showed mercy did. The story is about helping the man in front of you.
